phases.name: Route global requests
phases.description: Start from the global latency and availability goals, then place edge delivery and a stateless application runtime on the request path.

phases.name: Protect identity and data
phases.description: Separate authentication, relational source of truth, cache, and static-object delivery; do not let cached values become authoritative.

phases.name: Make change and health visible
phases.description: Represent schema migration as a controlled release concern and make the stated service objectives measurable.

phases.name: Connect request, release, and telemetry paths
phases.description: Connect the components in execution order and show cache misses, database changes, static delivery, and operational signals.

phases.name: Review the targets
phases.description: Treat the numeric goals as acceptance criteria to measure, not performance guarantees implied by a diagram.

steps.phase: Route global requests
steps.title: Freeze the exact problem brief
steps.content:
Title: Design a Scalable Global Web Application
Description: Design a web application that deploys globally, auto-scales based on traffic, serves content with low latency, and provides managed database services.
Requirements:
1. Deploy web application globally
2. Handle user authentication
3. Store relational data
4. Serve static assets efficiently
5. Auto-scale based on traffic
6. Implement caching strategies
7. Monitor application health
8. Handle database migrations
Constraints:
1. Page load time under 2 seconds
2. Support 100k+ concurrent users
3. 99.95% availability SLA
4. Global latency under 200ms
5. Cost-effective scaling
Hints:
1. App Engine for application hosting
2. Cloud SQL for relational database
3. Cloud Storage for static files
4. Cloud CDN for content delivery
5. Memorystore for caching
6. Cloud Monitoring for observability

steps.phase: Route global requests
steps.title: Choose a global request entry point
steps.content: Use a globally distributed HTTPS load-balancing boundary to terminate and route client requests toward healthy application backends. Regional failover and health checks support the availability goal, but the 99.95% target still needs an explicit SLI/SLO and failure testing.

component.label: Google Cloud Global Load Balancer
component.description: Global HTTPS entry and healthy-backend routing.

properties.purpose: Accept global HTTPS traffic, route to healthy application backends, and expose health and latency signals for regional failover evaluation.

component.highlightReason: The global deployment, availability, concurrency, and latency goals require an explicit entry and routing layer.

steps.phase: Route global requests
steps.title: Serve cacheable content near users
steps.content: Place an edge content-delivery layer on the static-content path. Keep immutable/versioned assets cacheable and define invalidation or versioned URLs for changes; dynamic authenticated responses should not be cached as public assets.

component.label: Cloud CDN
component.description: Edge delivery for cacheable static assets and eligible responses.

properties.purpose: Deliver versioned static assets from edge locations and forward cache misses toward the global application origin; exclude private or user-specific responses from public caching.

component.highlightReason: Cloud CDN is explicitly hinted and directly supports efficient static delivery and the page-load target.

steps.phase: Route global requests
steps.title: Keep the application tier stateless and elastic
steps.content: Represent the hinted App Engine-style managed application tier without fixing instance counts or regions. Externalize session state, expose readiness/health checks, and let measured demand drive scaling rather than assuming a capacity number from the brief.

component.label: Global Web Runtime (App Engine)
component.description: Stateless managed application handlers for web requests.

properties.purpose: Run stateless web handlers behind the global load balancer, externalize session state, expose health checks, and scale with observed demand; instance counts and deployment regions remain workload decisions.

component.highlightReason: The brief asks for global deployment and auto-scaling but does not state traffic shape or a fixed capacity.

steps.phase: Protect identity and data
steps.title: Make authentication an explicit boundary
steps.content: Keep credential validation and token/session policy separate from general application data access. The brief does not choose an identity provider, federation protocol, or session lifetime, so those remain deployment decisions.

component.label: User Authentication Service
component.description: Validates user identity and issues scoped application sessions.

properties.purpose: Authenticate users, validate session or token claims, and return identity context for authorization; identity provider and session lifetime are not specified.

component.highlightReason: Authentication is a functional requirement and must be visible as a trust boundary.

steps.phase: Protect identity and data
steps.title: Add cache-aside for hot, reconstructable reads
steps.content: Use Memorystore as a performance layer for frequently read, safely expiring data. The relational database remains authoritative; define key scoping, invalidation, and behavior on cache loss before relying on cache hit rates.

component.label: Memorystore (Redis)
component.description: Cache-aside acceleration for selected application reads.

properties.purpose: Cache hot, reconstructable application reads with bounded expiration; treat Cloud SQL as authoritative and define invalidation and cache-outage behavior.

component.highlightReason: Caching is explicit in the requirements and can reduce repeated regional database reads.

steps.phase: Protect identity and data
steps.title: Keep relational records in the managed source of truth
steps.content: Use the hinted Cloud SQL role for relational application records. Choose schema, indexes, connection pooling, backups, and read-replica strategy only after workload and consistency needs are known; do not treat replicas or caches as the write authority.

component.label: Cloud SQL Relational Database
component.description: Managed relational persistence for application records.

properties.purpose: Persist relational application records as the authoritative transactional store; engine, sizing, HA configuration, and replica topology require workload and recovery requirements.

component.highlightReason: The brief explicitly requires relational storage and hints Cloud SQL, while leaving the engine and capacity open.

steps.phase: Protect identity and data
steps.title: Store static objects separately from relational rows
steps.content: Use Cloud Storage for versioned static assets and large immutable objects. The application build can publish asset versions here; a CDN serves public cacheable objects while authorization remains at the application for private content.

component.label: Cloud Storage Static Assets
component.description: Durable object origin for versioned static files.

properties.purpose: Store versioned static build assets and large objects separately from relational rows; publish immutable asset names for safe edge caching and keep private-object access authorized.

component.highlightReason: Cloud Storage is hinted for static assets and avoids serving large immutable files through application instances.

steps.phase: Make change and health visible
steps.title: Version and gate database migrations with releases
steps.content: Treat schema changes as versioned deployment artifacts: validate compatibility, apply an ordered migration, then roll out code that depends on it. Use expand/contract changes when old and new application versions may overlap; rollback cannot assume a destructive schema change is reversible.

component.label: Application and Schema Release Pipeline
component.description: Build, test, migrate, and deploy compatible application versions.

properties.purpose: Build and test immutable application artifacts, run reviewed versioned schema migrations with compatibility checks, and deploy progressively; rollback and destructive migrations require explicit plans.

component.highlightReason: Database migrations are explicitly required and need a safe release boundary rather than ad hoc production edits.

steps.phase: Make change and health visible
steps.title: Measure user-visible health and backend saturation
steps.content: Collect request latency, error rate, availability, saturation, cache behavior, and migration health. The stated page-load and availability objectives need defined measurement boundaries, percentiles, user geography, and an alerting policy before they can be claimed as achieved.

component.label: Cloud Monitoring and SLOs
component.description: Service health, latency, saturation, and release telemetry.

properties.purpose: Observe edge and backend request latency, errors, saturation, cache and database health, and release/migration outcomes; define SLIs and alerts against the stated targets.

component.highlightReason: Monitoring is a requirement and provides evidence for the availability, page-load, concurrency, and latency targets.

steps.phase: Make change and health visible
steps.title: Keep unprovided capacity and latency details explicit
steps.content: The brief does not specify read/write mix, request-size distribution, geography, p95/p99 boundaries, database engine, recovery objectives, or traffic peaks. Preserve the provided thresholds as testable targets; size regions, autoscaling limits, cache TTLs, and SQL topology from measured workload rather than inventing them.

steps.phase: Connect request, release, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Forward edge cache misses to the global origin
steps.content: A cache miss or revalidation reaches the global routing layer; the CDN edge should serve eligible hits without making every asset request traverse application compute.

connection.label: cache misses and revalidation
connection.description: Cloud CDN forwards misses and revalidations to the global HTTPS load-balancing origin.

steps.phase: Connect request, release, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Route requests to healthy application backends
steps.content: Send dynamic and authenticated requests to healthy application instances. The global routing path reduces avoidable geographic distance but does not itself prove the under-two-second page-load target.

connection.label: route to healthy runtime
connection.description: Global health-aware routing sends application requests to available runtime backends.

steps.phase: Connect request, release, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Validate identity before protected operations
steps.content: The application delegates login or token validation to the authentication boundary and authorizes each protected operation using the returned identity context.

connection.label: authenticate and authorize
connection.description: Application requests validate identity/session claims and apply authorization before protected data access.

steps.phase: Connect request, release, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Check the cache before repeated relational reads
steps.content: Use cache-aside only for selected keys: the application checks Redis, reads the source of truth on a miss, and fills the cache with an explicit expiry/invalidation policy.

connection.label: read hot values
connection.description: Application handlers use Memorystore for cache-aside reads of selected data.

steps.phase: Connect request, release, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Use Cloud SQL for authoritative relational reads and writes
steps.content: Persist transactions and uncached reads in Cloud SQL. Connection pooling, indexes, and replica routing must be tested at the concurrency target; failover and consistency behavior belong in the SLO evidence.

connection.label: relational reads and transactions
connection.description: The stateless runtime reads and writes authoritative relational records in managed Cloud SQL.

steps.phase: Connect request, release, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Refill cache from the authoritative database
steps.content: On a cache miss, load the needed value from Cloud SQL and repopulate Redis according to the chosen freshness policy. Cache loss must degrade performance, not erase durable state.

connection.label: miss reads source of truth
connection.description: Cache misses are reconstructed from Cloud SQL; database data remains authoritative.

steps.phase: Connect request, release, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Publish versioned static assets with each build
steps.content: The build pipeline publishes immutable static assets to Cloud Storage before application rollout; runtime handlers can issue authorized access for private objects without exposing them to a public shared cache.

connection.label: publish versioned static files
connection.description: The release pipeline uploads immutable static asset versions to Cloud Storage for CDN delivery.

steps.phase: Connect request, release, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Use Cloud Storage as the edge origin for static files
steps.content: Cloud CDN fetches cache misses from the versioned object origin; immutable names allow long-lived caching while new builds publish new asset versions.

connection.label: versioned static objects
connection.description: Cloud Storage supplies cacheable versioned objects to Cloud CDN as its static origin.

steps.phase: Connect request, release, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Deploy tested application versions progressively
steps.content: The release pipeline promotes immutable tested builds to the managed runtime and can stop or roll back on failed health checks. A canary percentage or rollout duration is intentionally unspecified.

connection.label: promote tested application build
connection.description: CI/CD deploys compatible tested application artifacts to the managed runtime.

steps.phase: Connect request, release, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Apply compatible migrations before dependent code
steps.content: A reviewed migration job updates schema in a backward-compatible sequence before dependent application code relies on it. Use expand/contract and explicit backup/restore procedures for high-risk changes.

connection.label: reviewed schema migration
connection.description: The release pipeline applies ordered, versioned, compatibility-checked migrations to Cloud SQL.

steps.phase: Connect request, release, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Measure edge availability and user-facing latency
steps.content: Capture global request outcomes and edge latency to compare regional user experience with the stated targets, using a defined percentile and measurement window.

connection.label: global request health
connection.description: Global routing exports availability, latency, and backend health signals for SLO evaluation.

steps.phase: Connect request, release, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Observe application latency, errors, and scaling
steps.content: Track request rate, latency, errors, instance scaling, and saturation so autoscaling decisions and user-visible objectives can be validated from real workloads.

connection.label: runtime SLI and scaling signals
connection.description: The application exports request, error, saturation, and scaling telemetry to Cloud Monitoring.

steps.phase: Connect request, release, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Alert on database saturation and migration outcomes
steps.content: Monitor connection saturation, query latency, storage growth, backup/failover health, and migration results. The brief gives an availability objective but no recovery time or recovery point target.

connection.label: database health and migration signals
connection.description: Cloud SQL health and release migration results are observable for reliability and SLO review.

steps.phase: Connect request, release, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Verify that caching improves rather than hides health
steps.content: Observe hit rate, evictions, stale data, and dependency errors. A high hit rate is not itself proof of correctness; test invalidation and cache outage behavior.

connection.label: cache effectiveness and errors
connection.description: Memorystore metrics reveal hit rate, eviction, and failure behavior without replacing correctness checks.

steps.phase: Review the targets
steps.title: Turn the brief's numbers into acceptance tests
steps.content: The 2-second page-load, 100k+ concurrency, 99.95% availability, and under-200ms global latency values are targets—not guarantees from the selected products. Define geography, measurement percentile, test duration, failure scenarios, cost envelope, and realistic traffic mix; then validate autoscaling, database capacity, cache correctness, and recovery under load.
